subject: botany_2
question_text: Explain the chemical structure of viruses.

mark_split.label: Number and form of the nucleic acid

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.28, printed question 27. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERROR, corrected on this card: the guide says the viral genome is "either single stranded DNA (or) double stranded DNA" and then, one line later, that plant viruses have ssRNA — which its own sentence has just excluded. A viral genome may be ssDNA, dsDNA, ssRNA or dsRNA; the card gives all four. The guide's flat claim that plant viruses have ssRNA and animal viruses dsDNA is also an over-generalisation and is written here as the usual case, not the rule.

insider_note: Core and capsid. Say those two words first, then everything else hangs off them. The capsomere is the word the examiner is scanning for.

steps.label: The two basic components
steps.margin_note: Both components named and defined. Add the word virion.
lines: Every virus consists of TWO basic components:
a) the CORE — the nucleic acid, which forms the
genome;
b) the CAPSID — the protein coat that surrounds
the core.
A complete virus particle is called a VIRION.
steps.why: A virus is nothing but genetic material in a protein box, which is why two components are enough to describe every one of them.
common_mistakes: Saying viruses have a cell membrane and cytoplasm. They have only a core and a capsid.
Calling the capsid the genome. The CORE is the genome; the capsid is protein.
steps.memory_tip: Core inside, capsid outside, virion is the whole thing.

steps.label: The capsid and capsomeres
steps.margin_note: Function, the subunit name, and the fact that the count is characteristic.
lines: The CAPSID gives the virus its shape and
protects the core.
It is made of protein subunits called
CAPSOMERES.
The NUMBER of capsomeres is a characteristic
feature of each type of virus.
In TMV there are 2,130 capsomeres.
steps.why: Because the capsomere count is fixed for each virus, it is one of the features used to identify and classify them.
common_mistakes: Calling the subunits capsids. The subunits are CAPSOMERES; the whole coat is the capsid.
Saying the capsid carries the genetic information. The CORE does.
steps.memory_tip: Capsid is the coat; capsomeres are the bricks it is built from.

steps.label: The genome
steps.margin_note: All four possibilities, then the usual cases for plants and animals.
lines: The genome of a virus may be:
single stranded DNA, double stranded DNA,
single stranded RNA, or double stranded RNA.
NO virus has both DNA and RNA.
Most PLANT viruses have single stranded RNA.
Many ANIMAL viruses have double stranded DNA.
steps.why: A virus carries only one kind of nucleic acid, which is the single sharpest chemical difference between a virus and a cell.
common_mistakes: Saying a virus can have both DNA and RNA. It has ONE of them, never both.
Giving only DNA. RNA viruses include TMV, polio and HIV. The guide's own answer contradicts itself here.
steps.memory_tip: One virus, one kind of nucleic acid.

steps.label: Number and form of the nucleic acid
steps.margin_note: Shape, number, and the named exception. Four lines.

lines.text: One kind of nucleic acid, never both

lines: The nucleic acid molecule may be CIRCULAR or
LINEAR.
Most viruses have a SINGLE nucleic acid
molecule.
A few have more than one: HIV has TWO identical
molecules of RNA.
steps.why: HIV carrying two copies of its RNA is the standard exception, which is why the question is worth asking at all.
common_mistakes: Saying every virus has one molecule. HIV has TWO identical RNA molecules.
Leaving out the shape. Circular or linear is part of this mark.
steps.memory_tip: Usually one molecule; HIV carries two.
